subject: Chemistry
topic: Electronic configurations of the d-block elements
title: d-Block Configurations: Why Chromium and Copper Break the Rule
summary: The d-block's general configuration is (n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns¹⁻², with 4s filling before 3d. Chromium (3d⁵4s¹) and copper (3d¹⁰4s¹) move one 4s electron into 3d, because 3d and 4s are very close in energy and half-filled and full d sets are extra stable.

notes.title: 03 – Electronic Configurations of the d-Block Elements

keyPoints: General outer configuration: **(n−1)d¹⁻¹⁰ ns¹⁻²**; 4s fills before 3d.
Why: 3d and 4s are **very close in energy**, and **d⁵ and d¹⁰ are extra stable** (exchange energy, symmetry).

sections.h: Why chromium and copper are different

list: The 3d and 4s orbitals are very close in energy, so a small extra stability decides the arrangement.
Half-filled (d⁵) and completely filled (d¹⁰) sets are extra stable: more exchange energy and a symmetrical distribution.
So one 4s electron moves into 3d: Cr 3d⁵4s¹, Cu 3d¹⁰4s¹.

blocks.p: In the 4d series palladium goes further: 4d¹⁰ 5s⁰.

quiz.q: General outer configuration of the d-block:
Cr and Cu break the filling order because:
options: d⁵ and d¹⁰ sets are extra stable
quiz.explain: With 3d and 4s close in energy, stability decides.
